items.html:
The root cause isn't an old toolchain. Advect's CI runs clippy with two different versions, the 1.94 minimum and the latest stable (1.99), and since 1.99 they disagree about this one attribute. Bumping to the latest toolchain doesn't fix that properly:

  • Bumping the minimum to 1.99 is the risky option. Advect documents "Rust 1.94 or newer", and 1.99 came out on Sep 28. Anyone building from source (the sdist, or the conda-forge recipe, which uses conda-forge's Rust compiler) would need a five-day-old Rust. That costs users something, just to silence a lint.
  • It also doesn't stop this from happening again. The stable lane will pick up 1.100's new lints the same way.

Recommended proper fix: run clippy only on stable, which still catches new lints first. Keep the 1.94 lane for build and test, so the minimum version is still checked. Then remove the redundant #[must_use] outright and update the one line in docs/development/testing.md that says clippy runs on both. This is about three small changes and removes the cause.

Alternative: keep what's pushed now. #[must_use] with a message is the same idiom std uses on its iterators; it passes both clippy versions, and nothing else changes.

Should I switch the Advect PR to the recommended fix, or keep the current one? Either way the minimum stays at 1.94.

The last bug is fixed, and PR #1 is green and ready to merge at 86c4b2d. CI settled with 42 checks passing, none failing, and the 2 deploy jobs skipped as usual on PRs. CI Success, both Codecov checks and the formal proofs pass.

What was wrong: with a traced input (JAX, PyTorch, Autograd or Advect), 1-D lattice sums got their output shape wrong. The code guessed whether a trailing (1, 1) period or (1,) Bloch number meant one lattice cell or a batch, and that's ambiguous. So kpar=[k] returned a scalar instead of shape (1,), and a [[p]] period returned a scalar instead of (1, 1). It affected every 1-D lattice sum, not just lsumsw1d and lsumcw1d.

The fix: traced 1-D sums now follow NumPy exactly. For the named sums such as lsumsw1d, any array shape is a batch. For lsumsw(1, …) and lsumcw(1, …), a (1, 1) period and a (1,) Bloch vector are one cell, as in the NumPy path. Values and gradients are unchanged, and the periodic-solve path is untouched.

Verified:

  • An independent check covered all 24 one-dimensional sum functions over 3,192 input combinations per framework. 1,602 differed from NumPy before the fix; with raw inputs, none do now, in shape, value or gradient.
  • A new test with 56 cases fails 36 of them without the fix and passes all of them with it.
  • The full local suite passes (6,599 passed, 22 expected skips), as do ruff and the generated-docs check.

Commits and state:

  • I folded the fix into the existing fix commit, so the PR is still five commits. That rewrote the last commit, so I force-pushed with a lease pinned to the old head (9211de3...86c4b2d).
  • The PR description is updated […], and your local checkout is synced to 86c4b2d.
  • The temporary worktree and build files are removed.

Not fixed: passing a Lattice or WaveVector into 1-D sums. The framework path accepts some combinations NumPy rejects, such as a Lattice with a Bloch number of shape (2, 1) or (3, 1). It also gives a different shape for the realsum, recsum and dsum 1-D sphere sums. Neither combination is a documented input for these functions, and both behaved this way before; I left them for after the release.

Still to do on your side: merge the PR. Before you release, check the date (2026-10-03) in CHANGELOG and CITATION.
